summary:
LunaBase — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

LunaBase is an educational game that lets players experience life on a lunar base. During a seven-day mission, players must manage water, oxygen, food, and energy to keep astronauts safe.

Players can explore the Moon, drive a rover, grow plants, solve problems, and complete scientific missions. The game also includes different difficulty levels, quizzes, and a bilingual Arabic-English interface.

LunaBase uses Python and Streamlit and aims to make learning about space exploration fun and simple for young learners.
details:
LunaBase — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

1. Project Summary

LunaBase is a bilingual educational lunar-base simulation game developed using Python and Streamlit. It allows young learners to experience the challenges of operating a lunar outpost through a seven-day mission.

Players manage essential resources, including water, oxygen, energy, food, and radiation protection, while conducting scientific activities and responding to emergencies. The project combines interactive gameplay, simplified engineering concepts, educational challenges, and real NASA space-weather observations to make space exploration more accessible.

2. Main Features

LunaBase offers four interactive environments: Exterior, Habitat, Emergency, and Rover.

Key features include:

• Seven-day lunar missions with three difficulty levels.
• Resource management involving water, oxygen, energy, food, and radiation protection.
• Interactive astronaut and rover drag-and-drop activities.
• Life-support monitoring and emergency scenarios.
• A greenhouse simulation inspired by published EDEN ISS research.
• Scientific exploration activities and educational quizzes.
• NASA DONKI solar-flare observations presented as educational information.
• A rule-based Mission Coach offering recommendations based on the player’s decisions and current game state.
• Mission reports and completion certificates.
• Full Arabic and English language support.

The main educational goal is to help students understand how engineering decisions and limited resources affect the sustainability of a lunar base.

3. NASA Data and Scientific Resources

NASA DONKI

LunaBase retrieves recent solar-flare observations through NASA’s DONKI API. These observations provide real-world space-weather context but do not directly control the simulator’s randomized solar-storm events.

Source: https://api.nasa.gov/

NASA Open Science Data Repository — OSD-895

The project references study OSD-895 / ALSDA LSDS-160 as a related scientific resource. Its archive files are not downloaded or processed by the application.

Source: https://osdr.nasa.gov/bio/repo/data/studies/OSD-895

EDEN ISS Research

Greenhouse crop-production reference values are based on the published research:

Zabel, P., Zeidler, C., Vrakking, V., Dorn, M., & Schubert, D. (2020). Biomass Production of the EDEN ISS Space Greenhouse in Antarctica During the 2018 Experiment Phase. Frontiers in Plant Science, 11, 656.

https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2020.00656

EDEN ISS was an Antarctic greenhouse research facility, not a lunar installation.

4. Technologies

• Python and Streamlit
• Pandas
• HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
• SVG-based interactive scenes
• NASA Open APIs
• Python unittest framework

5. Scientific Limitations

LunaBase is an independent educational prototype, not an operational lunar mission simulator. Resource consumption, engineering thresholds, and greenhouse mechanics are simplified game assumptions rather than validated spacecraft specifications.

NASA DONKI observations provide educational context and do not directly modify the simulation’s randomized events. The project is not an official NASA product.

6. AI Tools Disclosure

ChatGPT (OpenAI) was used to assist with troubleshooting, targeted code refinements, and documentation.

The in-game Mission Coach is rule-based and does not use a generative AI model.

7. Project Links

• Source Code: [https://github.com/amjed-x1u/lunabase--junior-astronaut]
